listings.title: Who Discovered Infrared Light?
listings.description:
William Herschel discovered infrared light in 1800, with a prism and thermometers.

Just beyond the red end of the visible spectrum, his thermometer grew warmer still. The light was invisible, but its warmth gave it away.

Sources:
Caltech IPAC, Herschel experiment: https://coolcosmos.ipac.caltech.edu/page/herschel_experiment
NASA, Infrared Waves: https://science.nasa.gov/ems/07_infraredwaves/

listings.title: How Was Phosphorus Discovered?
listings.description:
Hennig Brand discovered phosphorus while trying to find gold in urine in Hamburg in 1669.

He boiled it down to a black sludge. Instead of gold, he found a white substance that glowed in the dark.

Sources:
Hennig Brand biography: https://www.famousscientists.org/hennig-brand/
Los Alamos National Laboratory, Phosphorus: https://periodic.lanl.gov/15.shtml

listings.title: How Did John Snow Stop Cholera?
listings.description:
John Snow traced cholera deaths to the Broad Street water pump and had its handle removed.

In Soho, London, in 1854, many still blamed bad air. Snow tracked where the dead had lived: the deaths clustered around one pump.

Sources:
UCLA, Broad Street pump outbreak: https://epi-snow.ph.ucla.edu/Stream2_BSPoutbreak_a.html
UCLA, Removal of the pump handle: https://epi-snow.ph.ucla.edu/Stream2_BSPoutbreak_e.html

listings.title: Are Marie Curie's Notebooks Still Radioactive?
listings.description:
Yes. Marie Curie's notebooks are still radioactive, and her papers are kept in lead-lined boxes in Paris.

In 1898, Marie and Pierre Curie discovered polonium, then radium. This Short tells the story behind the notebooks.

Sources:
AIP, The discovery of radium: https://history.aip.org/history/exhibits/curie/resbr2.htm
ScienceAlert, Marie Curie personal effects: https://www.sciencealert.com/these-personal-effects-of-marie-curie-will-be-radioactive-for-another-1-500-years
